_comment: Labelled specimen set for the guard's precision/recall eval. NEGATIVES are verbatim excerpts of real documents that falsely tripped the PreToolUse never-reopen guard during the 2026-07-25 handoff-producer design session (pain-point #27). Each names the atom it wrongly fired, so a regression is legible. POSITIVES are generated from the live corpus by the eval itself (a query naming a killed option verbatim MUST fire), so recall is measured against all 500 atoms rather than a hand-picked few. Per d_23bf88 the eval runs against the real binding feed; a synthetic fixture is scale-lockable to whatever makes it pass.

negatives.name: api-route-segment
negatives.why_false: ADR-0050 renames the desktop GUI. This text is an API route. The option's pieces (keep/lema/workspaces) are common words that co-occur in any long lema document.
negatives.text: **Lift.** `syncOnBoundary` gains `syncHandoff`, a sibling of `syncCheckpoint`, firing on the existing boundary against the already-live `POST /workspaces/{id}/runs/{runID}/events` with `"kind": "handoff"`. No new endpoint. No migration. We keep the lema-run-state gate as-is, since that is the gate on the endpoint it POSTs to. Reading rides lema-state-brief. Both are env-wide WorkOS flags and both fail closed.

negatives.name: using-the-chosen-name
negatives.why_false: The killed option is the bare name 'Record' (rejected as ambiguous); the chosen name is 'The Record'. This text USES the approved name and the record_decision verb. Using a chosen name is not re-proposing the alternative it beat.
negatives.text: Judgment stays human. Automate draft, cluster, recommend — never auto-accept into the Record. The moment a decision lands, record_decision it: the why plus the rejected alternative are the expensive things to reconstruct later. An unreviewed inference stays a draft, so a handoff line must be marked stated by the agent and unreviewed rather than rendered with the standing an accepted decision earned.

negatives.name: server-side-build-plan
negatives.wrongly_fired_key: Build it on the lema (server) side
negatives.why_false: d_3247c3 is about the collector omitting repo/branch on run-create. Every piece of its key (build/it/on/the/lema/server/side) is a common word; the conjunction is meaningless over a long document.
negatives.text: Order matters: build the read path first, so the producer has somewhere to land and you can seed a row by hand to test it. On the lema side that is a LatestLiveHandoff sibling plus a composer section; the server already accepts the kind, so there is no new endpoint and no migration. Then the producer, then the self-resolution fix.

negatives.name: pain-point-prose
negatives.why_false: Prose ABOUT the guard's false fires, quoting the decision it fired. Documenting a closed decision is the citation case the guard already tries to exempt, and it must not fire on the exemption's own subject matter.
negatives.text: The never-reopen guard fired false ruled_out eight times in one working session, across both matchers, and every fire was a bare token-overlap match against a decision that does not govern. A false not_ruled_out lets a bad idea through and a human catches it downstream; a false ruled_out stops correct work while asserting authority the record does not hold.

negatives.name: ordinary-english-linear
negatives.why_false: 'Linear' is a killed integration target AND an ordinary English adjective. Prose about linear scans must not read as re-proposing the Linear connector.
negatives.text: The matcher does a linear scan over the closed set for each edit, which is fine at this corpus size: five hundred atoms times a token-set lookup is microseconds, and the cost grows linearly rather than quadratically because the token set is built once per query.

negatives.name: ordinary-english-knowledge
negatives.why_false: 'Knowledge' is a killed name AND an ordinary noun this product's own vision prose uses constantly.
negatives.text: We are not building another place to store information, we are building the layer that makes a team's hard-won reasoning usable when it matters. That is knowledge the team already paid for, and it evaporates unless producing the record costs the human almost nothing.

negatives.name: public-record-identifiers
negatives.why_false: Every occurrence is a long-standing identifier in apps/api/internal/api/public_record.go (PublicRecord, GetRepoRecord, publicRepoRecordResponse) or the file's own doc prose. None introduces a surface named Record; the name predates the edit, which is what the baseline proves. Observed firing on EVERY edit to this file, 2026-07-30.

negatives.name: knowledge-audit-index
negatives.why_false: The index name jobs_one_active_knowledge_audit and the KindKnowledgeAudit const are pre-existing schema in apps/api/internal/jobs/jobs.go. An edit whose comment mentions them is not proposing Knowledge as a product surface.

negatives.name: guard-own-doc-comment
negatives.why_false: Prose describing the closed naming decision, with no citation marker to earn the citation exemption — so the naming gate alone must hold it. 'a durable body of knowledge' and 'the org-wide knowledge destination' are the ordinary noun, not a proposal to name a surface. Observed live while writing this very fix.
negatives.text: This gate applies only to single-token keys, the exposed class. The separating information is not in the key, it is in how the word occurs: a durable body of knowledge is not a proposal to name anything, and the org-wide knowledge destination already has a name.

positive_templates: I'm going to switch us to %s
we should just go with %s instead

positives.name: new-record-type
positives.why_true: Declares a brand-new exported type named Record in a file that never mentioned the word — the naming proposal the guard exists to catch.

positives.name: new-knowledge-route
positives.why_true: Introduces a new user-facing route and nav label named Knowledge. A route IS a surface name, and nothing in the file used the word before.

positives.name: rename-to-killed-name-prose
positives.why_true: An explicit prose proposal to adopt the killed name.
positives.text: Proposal: rename the destination to Knowledge across the product surface, since that reads plainer to new users.

positives.name: adopt-record-name-prose
positives.why_true: Names the killed option as the thing to call the surface — the use/mention line, on the mention side.
positives.text: We should just call the org-wide destination Record instead, and drop the article everywhere.
